clue.text: Person fiddling with cold radiator

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a radiator is a kind of heater

explanation.surface: Someone tinkering with a chilly radiator, trying to get the heating going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddling' reads as fixing the radiator, but here it means cheating, as in fiddling the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to swindle, so a person fiddling is a swindler or cheat.

clue.text: Get times to arrive first

parts.note: to come is to arrive
by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Instructions to fetch the arrival times before anyone else.

clue.text: Swear allegiance at the front, church getting cross out

parts.note: the opening letter of allegiance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but 'cross out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface writing is to rub it out or delete it, so it is a synonym for crossing out.

explanation.walkthrough: Tate Modern is London's modern art gallery, a fitting setting for this artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey Emin is a British artist, one of the Young British Artists and a Royal Academician.

clue.text: Two rivers meet in country

wordplay.note: R is the abbreviation for river, followed by the Ural, a river in Russia

explanation.surface: Two rivers joining somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is the adjective, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the countryside, which country means as an adjective.

clue.text: Handed-down information with name recalled

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: taken as written

definitions.text: which might be revealed in front

explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' is read as two U's, one dropped from each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleavage, the gap between breasts, may be on show at the front of a low-cut top.

clue.text: Criminals direct round over a Fed's head

clue.text: Stress about computing electronic score

clue.text: Blue tick's lost? Start to tweet series of unsatisfied experiences

parts.note: the first letter of tweet

clue.text: Queen after prince: very deviant

clue.text: Set out to pry, when neighbour originally comes in for a bit

explanation.definitionFit: A pennyworth is the amount a penny buys, so a small amount or a bit.

clue.text: Risking death by offending

clue.text: Dua Lipa, ignoring dad, secures conditions of being in two states

clue.text: American spirits found in bottles around conservative offices

clue.text: Out-of-date tin containing old leaves

taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Boy sent back hospital food
